summary: alelo-core preinstall exfiltrates environment variables and host identity to hardcoded IP
details: The preinstall.js lifecycle script, which runs automatically during npm install, collects the installer's hostname, username, platform, current working directory, and the entire process.env dictionary and POSTs the payload as JSON to https://209.99.185.109/preinstall with TLS certificate validation disabled (rejectUnauthorized:false). In CI/CD contexts process.env routinely contains cloud credentials (AWS_*), registry tokens (NPM_TOKEN), and CI tokens (GITHUB_TOKEN), so this constitutes bulk credential harvesting to a bare-IP, non-publisher endpoint. A stray helper file in the tarball also references the npm publisher account oxy12@proton.me, consistent with a malicious upload rather than a legitimate 'Alelo' project.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
